hard_fails: Reserved word 'validated' is used as a claim with no named external party and no citable output. Record table row 5 says 'Each comparison rests on a validated capture' (guardrail #3). Rewrite it as 'Each comparison uses a capture that passed the pose and framing checks'.
one_fix: In block 9, under the 'Not ready for a call?' line, add one line that links up and sideways: 'Other FitXpress programs:' followed by links to two live sibling FitXpress vertical pages (for example the BMI verification page and one other live /fitxpress/for-{vertical}/ page), plus a link to /fitxpress/ once that URL stops returning a 301 to the homepage.

lost_points.proof_of_belonging: The page has no fitness proof point and no customer logos, and the only deployment proof comes from weight-management and BMI-verification workflows; it never addresses connected-fitness hardware or class platforms despite the URL, and it names no buyer title.
lost_points.claims_discipline: Reserved word in 'validated capture'; the problem block's opening cause ('the app loses the subscription before the results arrive') is stated without a source; 'only FitXpress' leaves out the white-label scanning SDK category a fitness buyer actually evaluates; body-composition changes are sold (table row 2, hero mock lean +1.2 kg) while the page admits it has no accuracy or repeatability figure for body composition; BMI and BMR are called 'measured data'; identifiers called 'anonymized' are then mapped to member accounts, which makes them pseudonymous.
lost_points.sales_argument: The page never shows that the churn statistics are caused by a flat weight line (the Kidman 'lack of personalization' finding is a stretch); the accuracy block opens with a lead-in, not the answer, and never ties under 1 cm repeatability to the 3.4 cm change the hero sells; the price has no conclusion (cost per scan against a retained subscription); the comparison has 4 rows, 3 of them reading 'Depends on'; the one-line recommended setup is missing from How it works; visible copy is about 1,315 words, over the 1,300 budget.
lost_points.uniqueness_vs_parent: The accuracy, data-handling and pricing blocks, about 35% of the copy, are boilerplate shared across FitXpress pages; the fact sheet does not show the parent's Yoast title or description, so the difference is unverified; the definitional 'body scan at the gym' FAQ leans toward the hub article's intent.
lost_points.conversion: Analytics events are not verified on this page; 'Request a sample payload' leads to the demo-booking form, so the label does not match the action; the pilot's cost and commitment are not stated.
lost_points.buyer_language: Connected-fitness vocabulary (equipment, classes, workouts) is missing; 'payload' is engineering jargon for a Founder, CPO or Head of Growth; several sentences have things acting ('Two smartphone photos return', 'nutrition plans adjust', 'the paid tier can carry'); the H2 'the change the scale can't' is conversational; 'Pro' appears before it is introduced, and 'for the paid tier' could mean the app's tier or FitXpress Pro.
lost_points.human_copy: The detector reports clean and the page has an opinion and a boundary, but the 'the scale' motif appears three times, and every block repeats the same cadence (a table, then a verdict line, then a three-item list), so the page reads like a filled-in kit template; no 'what still reads as machine-written?' self-check is visible, which caps this axis at 8.
lost_points.search_ai_visibility: FAQPage schema is not validated; 3 of 4 FAQ answers partly restate the pilot, comparison or How it works blocks, and the onboarding answer deflects instead of answering; the focus keyphrase 'gym body scanner' attracts hardware buyers rather than app buyers, and 'connected fitness' barely appears in the body copy.
lost_points.place_and_technical: There are no sibling-vertical links and no in-body link up to /fitxpress/, which still returns a 301 to the homepage, so the breadcrumb's middle level depends on that page shipping; v3 has no prototype; 768 and 1440 px, contrast and keyboard operation are unmeasured; schema is not validated.
